description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

About the Team

As a Senior Threat Intelligence Engineer focused on Actor Analysis, you will investigate the cyber adversaries relevant to CoreWeave’s global cloud infrastructure, AI platform, and corporate environment. You will develop a detailed understanding of their objectives, capabilities, targeting patterns, infrastructure, and operational behavior, and assess how their activities could affect CoreWeave.

You will be part of CoreWeave’s defensive security operations team, working alongside threat hunters, detection engineers, incident responders, and other security engineers. You will conduct original research using external intelligence, technical artifacts, and internal telemetry, and apply your findings to active investigations, hunt hypotheses, deception capabilities, vulnerability prioritization, and detection improvements. Your research priorities will be driven by operational needs and gaps in our understanding of adversaries. Success means helping the security team identify threats, make better defensive decisions, and respond effectively.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain sustained coverage of priority cyber threat actors, including state-sponsored groups and cybercriminal organizations, tracking changes in their objectives, capabilities, targeting, and tradecraft relevant to CoreWeave.
  • Investigate adversary campaigns and intrusion activity to reconstruct operational timelines, identify attacker objectives, and assess implications for CoreWeave’s infrastructure, technologies, and business.
  • Research adversary infrastructure, tooling, malware, and operational patterns. Correlate technical artifacts and behaviors across external reporting, internal investigations, and telemetry to identify relationships between activity clusters and campaigns.
  • Develop and test hypotheses about actor relationships and attribution, accounting for shared infrastructure, commonly used tools, and alternative explanations. Clearly communicate supporting evidence, uncertainty, and confidence.
  • Produce actor profiles, campaign assessments, and intrusion analyses that help security teams make specific defensive decisions. Explain likely adversary actions, relevant attack paths, and opportunities to improve defenses.
  • Define intelligence requirements and collection gaps for priority actors in partnership with security teams. Pursue relevant information through open sources, commercial intelligence, research communities, and internal telemetry.
  • Support active investigations with Incident Response and Detection and Response, providing adversary context, investigative pivots, and assessments of campaign connections to inform triage, incident scope, and response decisions.
  • Develop actor-specific hunt hypotheses and participate in hunts with security partners. Translate observed behaviors into detection requirements and help detection engineers validate coverage against relevant adversary techniques.
  • Partner with security engineers to develop deception capabilities informed by actor targeting and tradecraft. Analyze activity from honeypots, canaries, decoys, and other instrumentation to refine actor assessments and identify new collection opportunities.
  • Assess observed exploitation and actor capabilities against CoreWeave’s technologies and exposure. Support vulnerability management by identifying adversary-relevant vulnerabilities and attack paths that warrant remediation priority.
  • Develop scripts and analytical workflows to enrich artifacts, track infrastructure, and correlate activity. Maintain actor relationships and supporting evidence in the threat intelligence platform, incorporating findings from defensive operations into ongoing research.

Qualifications:

  • 8–10 years of experience in cyber threat intelligence, security research, incident investigation, threat hunting, or related disciplines, with substantial experience conducting threat actor and campaign analysis.
  • Deep expertise in at least one cyber threat actor set, such as Chinese, Russian, Iranian, North Korean, or cybercriminal actors, demonstrated through sustained analysis of their campaigns, targeting, tradecraft, and infrastructure.
  • Demonstrated ability to produce original adversary research from technical evidence and multiple intelligence sources.
  • Deep understanding of adversary tradecraft, including initial access, credential theft, persistence, lateral movement, command and control, and infrastructure use.
  • Experience correlating intrusion activity, infrastructure, tooling, and targeting patterns to evaluate campaign relationships and attribution hypotheses.
  • Hands-on experience querying and analyzing endpoint, network, identity, or cloud telemetry to investigate adversary activity.
  • Demonstrated experience applying actor research to threat hunting, deception, vulnerability prioritization, detection engineering, or incident response, with concrete examples of resulting defensive improvements.
  • Strong analytical judgment, including source evaluation, consideration of competing hypotheses, and clear expression of uncertainty and confidence. Ability to explain technical findings and their operational implications to security teams and leadership.
  • Ability to independently manage actor research while adjusting priorities to support investigations, emerging threats, and other defensive requirements.

Preferred Skills:

  • Deep experience investigating state-sponsored actors or cybercriminal groups targeting cloud providers, technology companies, or the AI ecosystem.
  • Experience analyzing threats involving Linux, Kubernetes, cloud control planes, identity systems, or software supply chains.
  • Background in malware analysis, digital forensics, network analysis, or incident response.
  • Experience researching adversary infrastructure using passive DNS, certificate data, domain registration records, or other technical datasets.
  • Proficiency with Python, SQL, APIs, or graph analysis to support research and correlation.
  • Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK, intrusion analysis frameworks, and intelligence platforms used to maintain actor and campaign relationships.
  • Relevant certifications, such as GCTI, GCIH, or CTIA, are a plus.

The base salary range for this role is $182,000 to $242,000. The starting salary will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location. We strive for both market alignment and internal equity when determining compensation. In addition to base salary, our total rewards package includes a discretionary bonus, equity awards, and a comprehensive benefits program (all based on eligibility). 

What We Offer

In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a variety of benefits to support your needs. The benefits below reflect our US-based offerings for full-time employees; for roles in other locations, benefits vary and are shared during the hiring process. These include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance - 100% paid for by CoreWeave
  • Company-paid Life Insurance 
  • Voluntary supplemental life insurance 
  • Short and long-term disability insurance 
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • Health Savings Account
  • Tuition Reimbursement 
  • Ability to Participate in Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)
  • Mental Wellness Benefits through Spring Health 
  • Family-Forming support provided by Carrot
  • Paid Parental Leave 
  • Flexible, full-service childcare support with Kinside
  • 401(k) with a generous employer match
  • Flexible PTO
  • Catered lunch each day in our office and data center locations
  • A casual work environment
  • A work culture focused on innovative disruption

Equal Opportunity & Accommodations

CoreWeave is an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive workplace. All qualified applicants and candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information.

As part of this commitment and consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), CoreWeave will ensure that qualified applicants and candidates with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations for the hiring process, unless such accommodation would cause an undue hardship. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please contact: careers@coreweave.com.

Export Control Compliance

This position requires access to technology and/or source code subject to U.S. export control laws. Any such access will be provided only in compliance with applicable U.S. export control requirements. As part of the recruitment process, CoreWeave may request limited information reasonably necessary to assess applicable export-control requirements.
